title: Tommie Harris: OU's Lombardi Winner and a Three-Time Pro Bowler
question: How many Pro Bowls did former Oklahoma defensive tackle Tommie Harris make with the Chicago Bears?
answer: Three. Tommie Harris (OU 2001-03), the 2003 Lombardi Award winner, went 14th overall to the Chicago Bears in 2004 and made three straight Pro Bowls, in 2005, 2006 and 2007.
summary: Sooner DT Tommie Harris won the 2003 Lombardi Award, went 14th overall to Chicago and made three straight Pro Bowls. A look at his OU and NFL career highlights.
body: Tommie Harris (OU 2001-03) made his first college play in the 2001 opener against North Carolina and quickly became the kind of interior lineman offensive coordinators lose sleep over. He was a two-time All-American for Bob Stoops, a Lombardi Award finalist as a sophomore and the winner as a junior.

The Lombardi story has a nice twist. In 2002 Harris finished runner-up to Arizona State's Terrell Suggs. A year later he won it outright, becoming the 12th Oklahoma player named a finalist and only the third Sooner to take home the trophy, joining a club that includes Lee Roy Selmon from 1975. Harris also declined to vote for himself, saying it just would not have been right.

Leaving after his junior year, he went 14th overall to the Chicago Bears in 2004. He made three consecutive Pro Bowls, in 2005, 2006 and 2007, as a quick, disruptive presence in the middle of the Chicago defense.

Harris spent seven seasons in Chicago and one with the San Diego Chargers. Across 117 NFL games, 91 of them starts, he posted 231 tackles, 56 tackles for loss, 31.5 sacks and an interception, a strong résumé for an interior lineman.
